title: Scott Parker departs Burnley after Premier League relegation
content:
Scott Parker has left Burnley by mutual consent following the club’s relegation from the Premier League.

Burnley confirmed in a statement Mike Jackson, previously caretaker at the end of the 2021-22 season following Sean Dyche’s exit, will take charge for the club’s remaining four games of the league campaign.

Burnley’s relegation back to the Championship was sealed following last week’s defeat at home to Manchester City with the club 16 points behind West Ham United with just 12 points left to play for.

“I have enjoyed every moment of our journey together, but feel that now is the right time for both parties to move in a different direction,” Parker said in a statement, shared on the club’s media.

“It was a true honour to lead this team into the Premier League.”

Parker was appointed in the summer of 2024 after Vincent Kompany’s move to Bayern Munich, and led the club to a second-place Championship finish with 100 points and just 16 goals conceded in 46 league games.

However, Burnley have been unable to replicate their defensive solidity in the Premier League; Parker’s side have conceded a league-high 68 goals this term.

Burnley won three of their opening nine Premier League matches, with home victories over Sunderland and Leeds United followed by an away win at Wolves. However, a 3-2 win at Crystal Palace in February has been their only top-flight victory since October, seeing them cut adrift alongside Wolverhampton Wanderers, who have also been relegated from the top flight.

Parker won promotion to the Premier League with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, but has been unable to replicate that success in English football’s top division. He has overseen relegations at Fulham and Burnley in those first seasons back, while Bournemouth parted company with him after a 9-0 defeat at Liverpool, the fourth matchday of the 2022-23 season.

Burnley still have four league games remaining, with visits to Leeds United (May 1) and Arsenal (May 17) either side of a home game against Aston Villa (May 10), before they host Wolves on the final day of the season, on May 24.

Analysis by The Athletic’s Andrew Jones

Parker’s time in charge at Burnley coming to an end felt like an inevitability.

After relegation was confirmed last week, it felt discussions that were held between the club’s hierarchy and head coach would end with a parting of ways.

After successfully steering Burnley to automatic promotion last season, Parker was unable to inspire a survival campaign and the club are currently on a run which has seen just one win in 25 Premier League matches.

Not all of Burnley’s fanbase was convinced by Parker’s pragmatic approach last season and performances and results this term has seen frustration from supporters towards Parker increasingly grow.

Burnley’s search for a new head coach has already begun and it is the third successive time they are preparing for a season in the Championship while hunting for a new coach.

Vincent Kompany and Parker both navigated their return to the Premier League via different styles and the same pressure will be on their next appointment  It also remains to be seen what type of head coach Burnley want. Kompany played free-flowing football while Parker was more defensive-focused.
